Data Preprocessing and Feature Engineering for Data Mining: Techniques, Tools, and Best Practices
results.content: *   [Conceptual Framework: A Context-Aware Taxonomy of Data Preprocessing and Feature Engineering](https://www.mdpi.com/2673-2688/6/10/257#sec2-ai-06-00257). Preprocessing involves a set of operations, including data cleaning, transformation, normalisation, feature encoding, and DR [[1](https://www.mdpi.com/2673-2688/6/10/257#B1-ai-06-00257),[4](https://www.mdpi.com/2673-2688/6/10/257#B4-ai-06-00257)]. For example, in [[5](https://www.mdpi.com/2673-2688/6/10/257#B5-ai-06-00257)], the authors discuss how various ML pipeline stages can introduce or mitigate bias, while preprocessing facilitates automation within the data pipelines, further contributing to increased reproducibility, scalability, and transferability in application scenarios. We propose a unifying framework ([Section 2](https://www.mdpi.com/2673-2688/6/10/257#sec2-ai-06-00257)), which systematically organises data preprocessing and feature engineering into five pipeline stages (cleaning, transformation, construction, selection, reduction), while explicitly linking them to decision criteria (dataset size, interpretability, domain constraints, computational resources). Because there is no domain-agnostic standard, we adopt a task-driven protocol: (i)diagnose influence (e.g., leverage, Cook’s distance) and distinguish data errors from rare-but-valid events [[42](https://www.mdpi.com/2673-2688/6/10/257#B42-ai-06-00257)]; (ii) compare treatments—retain, transform (e.g., log/winsorise) or remove—using CV on task metrics (ROC-AUC, RMSE) and stability across folds; (iii) select the least complex treatment that improves performance without degrading calibration or fairness; (iv) document decisions and parameters for audit [[24](https://www.mdpi.com/2673-2688/6/10/257#B24-ai-06-00257),[38](https://www.mdpi.com/2673-2688/6/10/257#B38-ai-06-00257)].
